speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To better understand the pattern of your weakness, does the difficulty climbing stairs worsen when you climb down or up, and does the double vision change when you look left, right, up, or down?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very telling for a neuromuscular condition. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Phosphokinase. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation. How long have you noticed these symptoms starting?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your normal CPK and nerve stimulation results, do you have any history of thyroid issues, or does your double vision disappear completely when you close one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.
